description.html: Lateralis, also known as the red runner or Turkestan roach, is smaller and faster than the dubia. Its constant movement triggers the hunting instinct, so it is excellent for chameleons, young geckos and lizards that only react to moving prey, as well as for fussy animals that refuse slower food. It is soft-bodied and easy to digest.

Nymphs suit babies and smaller species, and adults suit larger lizards and adult agamas. The size rule applies here too: the insect should not be wider than the space between the animal's eyes. Because of their speed, they are easiest to offer from a smooth-sided bowl or with tweezers, so they do not hide around the terrarium.

Lateralis cannot climb smooth glass or plastic, so it is easy to keep in a ventilated box with egg cartons in a warm place. Feed it vegetables, fruit and dry food, and dust it with calcium before feeding, occasionally with a multivitamin. Read more about choosing live food on our lizard food page.
